title: Pressure canning low-acid foods
h1: Pressure canning low-acid foods: validated processes, not internet shortcuts
dek: Why meat and vegetables need a pressure canner, what makes a home-canning process tested, and what the CDC, USDA and NCHFP say about the shortcuts that circulate online. A guide to the rules, not a recipe.
description: Why low-acid foods need a pressure canner, what makes a canning process validated, and what CDC, USDA and NCHFP say about multi-cookers, dry canning and shortcuts.
recheck: Immediately if the CDC, NCHFP or the USDA Complete Guide to Home Canning revises guidance on canners, multi-cookers or the boil-before-eating rule; otherwise at the next quarterly source sweep.

source_use.food-cdc-home-canned: Pressure canning is the only recommended method for low-acid foods; no boiling water canner or electric multi-cooker; use USDA recipes only; canner and gauge advice; storage; boil-before-eating rule; signs of contamination; if in doubt throw it out.
source_use.cdc-botulism-prevention: Toxin cannot be seen, smelled or tasted; if in doubt throw it out.
source_use.food-nchfp-ensuring-safe: Botulism growth conditions; definition and examples of low-acid foods; 240 to 250 F in pressure canners; the 20 to 100 minute and 7 to 11 hour time ranges; elevation.
source_use.food-nchfp-recommended-canners: Temperature versus pressure; trapped air and elevation as the two errors; gauge accuracy and Extension gauge testing; small pressure saucepans.
source_use.food-nchfp-using-pressure-canners: Canner types and size; venting 10 minutes; gauge accuracy; restart timing if pressure drops; do not force-cool; burner limits; handling cautions; directory of local experts.
source_use.nchfp-pressure-ground-meat: The example of a tested process: preparation, separate tables by jar size, gauge type and elevation band (not reprinted).
source_use.food-nchfp-multicooker: Why NCHFP does not support USDA processes in electric multi-cookers.
source_use.food-nchfp-dry-canning: Why canning raw vegetables without liquid is hazardous; processes must be used as written.
source_use.food-nchfp-not-recommended: Oven, microwave, dishwasher, open-kettle and dry-oven canning not recommended; canning powders useless.
source_use.food-nchfp-steam-canning: Atmospheric steam canning is endorsed for high-acid foods only.
source_use.food-usda-canning-guide-1: Spoiled low-acid food may show little evidence; handling suspect jars; storage and freezing of canned food.
source_use.food-fsis-shelf-stable: Botulism symptoms and timing; the boil-before-eating qualification; the conflicting storage chart row; double-bagging suspect cans.
source_use.food-osu-survival-food: Do not can water, butter, dairy, grains, leftovers, cakes, quick breads or cured meats; vacuum-sealing low-acid foods; canning during a long outage.
source_use.food-usu-canned-goods: Commercially canned is superior for storage; tasting and boiling advice that conflicts with CDC; do not let jars freeze.
source_use.food-fsis-emergencies: Discard home-canned food that touched floodwater.
source_use.food-cdc-after-emergency: Discard home-canned food that touched floodwater.
source_use.nchfp-home: What the National Center for Home Food Preservation is and says it provides.
